ideas.title: Wind the field coil yourself
ideas.critique: This is the open stator step, and it puts a real nonlinear FEM with saturation in the player's hands as a craft. Turns against wire resistance against saturation gives a genuine optimum, and the shunt-or-series choice adds depth. It collapses into a slider if 'holding a key per layer' only bumps N while the hands mime it. It is also another drum-motor post unless the film shows the winding changing what the cart does on the planks.

ideas.title: Crank against the load you chose
ideas.critique: This is round 1's crank with the glowing wire swapped for the pots, and it keeps the part that counted: torque from the hand, Lenz coming back through the circuit solver, and real recharge. Refilling the cart's own store is a goal the player can use. The weak spots are that a Jump-in key for force is a thin body for 'Lumi leaning into it', and a crank getting heavy is hard to read on film unless the hand and the speed visibly fight.

ideas.title: Lean on the lever down the dune
ideas.critique: A continuous lever that trades charge against belt slip on the real crest is a skill with an edge to it, and it turns s178's finding that the belt slips into something to play, not a bug. The capstan law plus generator torque is a one-axis cart model, though, so its realism depends on whether the slip and the squeal really come from the solve. The greedy-and-held film needs the belt visible, or it is a cart rolling down sand twice.
